transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-20
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Sanjay Mehta (Redwood AE), Claire Huang (Redwood SE), Maya Torres (Verdant Procurement), Ethan Park (Verdant SecOps), Leah Kim (Verdant PM)
Links referenced: procurement packet (internal), MSA draft v3: https://redwood.app/docs/msa/draft-v3, pilot deck: https://redwood.app/decks/verdant-accreditation

Auto-summary:
- Goal: agree onboarding sprint scope, clarify SLA fallbacks, and confirm what Verdant needs for procurement sign-off (KMS, SOC2, DPA language).
- Outcome: Redwood to send redlines + pilot plan; Verdant to confirm timeline and provide compliance artifact list.

Topics:
1) MSA/DPA redlines and data residency clauses
2) SLA tiers, rollback/fallback behavior and canary windows
3) Pilot scope: Dedicated vs Hosted, KMS options, connectivity (VPC), perf benchmarks
4) Compliance artifacts and procurement timeline

Transcript:
[00:00] Sanjay: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, um we set aside 45 minutes, I think, maybe 50 — just walk through the accreditation sprint and the SLA fallback scenario. Claire and I will run through the tech bits, legal bits we'll aim to capture redlines.
[00:18] Maya: Thanks Sanjay, appreciate it. Quick note — procurement committee wants a crisp list of docs and a fallback SLO if we can't hit dedicated throughput in first 30 days.
[00:30] Claire: yeah, understood. For us fallback typically means routing to a lower-cost hosted variant with clear latency bounds and token cost implications. we can show the routing policy.
[00:45] Ethan: when you say hosted variant, is data still staying in our VPC? like, we have regs about egress, we can't have PII leave region.
[00:58] Sanjay: good callout. So Redwood Private (or "Red wood Private" in some notes) is the on-prem/VPC option — sorry transcription, ha — that keeps data inside your cloud account. fallback path would only route to hosted if you opt-in and sign off on egress terms in the DPA.
[01:20] Leah: timelinewise, procurement wants sign-off by Sept 10 to hit a production rollout in October. is that realistic?
[01:35] Claire: technically yes, if we get pilot credentials and connectivity this week or next. the perf runs take a couple days each and we usually do a canary for 7-14 days depending on traffic shape.
[01:50] Maya: procurement needs a clear SLA table: availability, p99 latency, and credits for non-compliance. also a KMS keying narrative — we use a customer-managed key (CMK) with HSM.
[02:05] Sanjay: we can provide a table. question: are you looking for monthly uptime SLAs or per-route SLOs?
[02:15] Maya: prefer per-route SLOs for critical inference routes and an overall availability SLA for the platform.
[02:25] Claire: ok. quick technical note: if you pick Dedicated, you get reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput; we can set per-route p99 latency targets based on batch config. if you pick hosted-with-fallback we set a weighted routing policy and automatic fallback to a compatible quantized variant — that may increase latency ~10-30ms and change per-token cost.
[02:50] Ethan: something about KV cache and session affinity — will fallback drop user session context? that's a user-impact risk.
[03:02] Claire: good question. if the routing goes to a different model instance family we preserve KV cache for pinned sessions using prefix caching, but there is a small window where short-term context miss occurs. we'll document the exact behavior — and there's an option to warm the cache during canary.
[03:25] Sanjay: i'll add that to the redline notes, because procurement and product want the customer-impact language.
[03:35] Maya: on the DPA, we need strict locale/residency language and an egress fee clause if hosted fallback is used. also add audit log retention and access controls.
[03:48] Sanjay: agreeable. for egress fee we can propose a pass-through model — we should propose numbers. Claire, can you share cost delta between dedicated and hosted variants for the pilot?
[03:58] Claire: yes, i'll prepare a cost table — approximate numbers: dedicated reserved instance baseline, burst pricing, and hosted per-token. i'll attach to the MSA redline.
[04:12] Leah: security will need SOC2 Type II and a short architecture diagram showing key boundaries (KMS, ingress egress, audit trails).
[04:22] Ethan: also need to confirm SSO/SAML integration and RBAC so only service accounts used by our ops teams can call inference endpoints.
[04:32] Sanjay: we support SAML/SCIM and granular API keys with scoped routes. we'll share a SSO integration guide.
[04:40] Maya: procurement also asked about termination and data deletion — how fast can you purge customer data and can we get a signed attestation?
[04:52] Claire: for Redwood Private with customer KMS we can confirm deletion within 24-72 hours depending on replication; for hosted we have a standard deletion window we can commit to in DPA. we'll include attestation language in the DPA redline.
[05:05] Ethan: on KMS — we need a key rotation narrative and HSM proof. do you support customer-managed keys in cloud KMS (e.g. AWS KMS) and HSM-backed keys?
[05:17] Claire: yes — both. we have integrations with major KMS providers and can accept an external HSM if required for on-prem deployments.
[05:27] Maya: sounds good. Another procurement ask: competitor carveouts. they asked if you have exclusive clauses or forward-compatibility with other vendors.
[05:35] Sanjay: we don't require exclusivity. we mentioned GoliathAI earlier in procurement comparisons; i'm happy to provide a quick buyer's checklist that compares common tradeoffs.
[05:46] Leah: for the pilot, scope suggestion: two routes, one high-volume short-seq (chat completions) and one long-seq batch (document summarization). run with sample traffic for 6 hours each, collect p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens.
[06:01] Claire: that's a good plan. we'll configure batching and quantization profiles so the runs reflect production shapes.
[06:10] Maya: does the pilot require a signed MSA? procurement wants legal docs upfront but will accept a pilot amendment.
[06:19] Sanjay: usually we sign a pilot order form plus an MSA skeleton; redlines can be circulated in parallel — procurement can accept a pilot amendment to proceed.
[06:31] Ethan: regarding logging, we need immutable audit logs for admin actions and token-level access logs for 90 days. is that doable?
[06:42] Claire: yes, logging levels are configurable in Console, and we can forward logs to your SIEM. note there may be additional retention costs. we'll include expected retention and cost in the packet.
[06:58] Maya: about SLA credits — procurement requested an objective credit table (percent credit per downtime tier). do you have a template?
[07:07] Sanjay: yes we have a standard SLA credit schedule; for enterprise contracts we can negotiate tiers. i'll include the default table in the redline.
[07:17] Leah: one more technical q: how do you handle model rollouts and regressions — we'd like canary rollback triggers based on accuracy regressions for a sample eval set.
[07:29] Claire: Redwood Optimize supports eval-driven rollback. you can supply evaluation prompts and thresholds; we can set automatic rollback + notification. we'll want to know the exact eval set.
[07:39] Maya: procurement and legal also want indemnification language and limits on liability — what are standard Redwood positions?
[07:48] Sanjay: standard tech vendor positions: liability capped at fees paid in the prior 12 months with carveouts for gross negligence. of course, we can discuss specifics in legal redlines.
[07:59] Ethan: one minor thing — network egress fees. if fallback to hosted involves inter-region transfer, procurement will want clarity on who pays.
[08:10] Sanjay: we'll propose an egress table: customer pays egress when data leaves their VPC, Redwood covers internal routing within region for Dedicated. specifics in DPA.
[08:21] Maya: ok. next steps then?
[08:24] Sanjay: Claire and I will produce the MSA/DPA redline with the SLA table, provide the cost delta, and send a pilot runbook. Verdant will confirm procurement committee dates and send compliance artifacts.
[08:35] Leah: i'll compile the eval prompts and share them with Claire by end of week.
[08:42] Ethan: i'll send the security artifacts list, including required HSM certs, and confirm SSO user map.
[08:49] Sanjay: great. i'll target to circulate the MSA redline by Aug 24. Claire will share cost and runbook by Aug 25.
[08:58] Maya: sounds good, thanks all.
[09:02] (crosstalk briefly)
[09:05] Sanjay: any final questions?
[09:08] Maya: none from me.
[09:10] Claire: just one quick note — on the pilot we recommend a small canary before the big run to warm caches. avoids a noisy regress.
[09:18] Leah: agreed.
[09:20] Sanjay: perfect. we'll follow up via email and drop the packet into the procurement folder you shared: https://verdantlabs.share/rdw-procurement
[09:30] End meeting.

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-hearings (Redwood sometimes transcribed as Red wood, KV cache shown as K-V cache), filler words preserved.
